name: intxt
title: Anonymous Intention-Tagged Messaging
description: Anonymous messaging where senders tag the intention of each message. The tag shows on the message itself, so meaning is never misread.
audience: Anyone who has been misunderstood in text — remote workers, couples, friends, managers, or anyone in a situation where a message could land wrong without the right context.
useCases: A manager sends critical feedback to a remote employee — tags it 'sincere' so the intent is clear before the words are read
Two friends are bantering over text — one tags a sharp reply 'joking' so it doesn’t accidentally start a fight
Someone needs a hard conversation but wants anonymity — creates a chat with a random code and shares the link, no accounts or phone numbers involved
A couple resolves a disagreement over text — intention tags prevent the 'are you being sarcastic?' spiral by making meaning visible upfront

dataPrivacy.storage: Messages stored in cloud database for delivery. Identity is a random device ID — no email, phone, or account.
dataPrivacy.authentication: Anonymous. Random UUID generated on first launch, stored securely on device.
dataPrivacy.deletion: Uninstalling the app permanently deletes your identity. No recovery, no backdoors.
dataPrivacy.security: Row-level security policies. Anti-spam rate limiting and auto-flagging. Anonymous reporting for moderation.
dataPrivacy.thirdParty: Supabase for database and realtime. Web Push (VAPID) for notifications.
